The *Vessabhūbuddhavaṁsa* (Bv 23) is a canonical poetic narrative situated within the *Buddhavaṁsa* in the Khuddaka Nikāya of the Pali Tipiṭaka [SuttaCentral]. Titled *The History of the Buddha Vessabhū* in modern English translation, the chapter recounts the life, awakening, and biographical particulars of Vessabhū, the twenty-second of the twenty-four previous Buddhas preceding Gotama Buddha [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records two modern translations of the text in two languages [SuttaCentral].

Text-reuse analysis conducted by DharmaNexus indicates extensive overlap between this text and the *Buddhavaṁsa-aṭṭhakathā*, with 72 matching passages and longest alignments covering segments §9.4–17.3 [DharmaNexus]. The work also exhibits standard formulaic recurrence characteristic of the *Buddhavaṁsa*, sharing repetitive biographical segments (especially around verses §19.1–25.2) with accounts of other Buddhas, including the *Phussabuddhavaṁsa* (Bv 20), *Sikhībuddhavaṁsa* (Bv 22), *Koṇāgamanabuddhavaṁsa* (Bv 25), *Atthadassībuddhavaṁsa* (Bv 16), and *Kakusandhabuddhavaṁsa* (Bv 24) [DharmaNexus]. Beyond Pali, DharmaNexus computes lower-level text-reuse alignments with Tibetan canonical texts, notably the Tibetan version of the *Jātakanidāna* (D0032) and Mahāyāna sūtras such as the *Samādhirājasūtra* (D0127) [DharmaNexus].
